purpose: Teach style-conditioned impulse buying with the frozen informed prompt; not human behavior evidence.
split_unit: base customer (all three style variants and both layouts stay together)
limitations: Labels come from a deterministic rule teacher, not people. The model learns these rules, not human impulse psychology.
Impulse depends on the visible impulse_buy_probability (tier: >=0.40 / >=0.20 / >=0.10 / none), diet/allergy/alcohol tags, health, department, price, budget slack, urgency and extras already taken.
Two of three style variants per base customer are counterfactual (same list and budget; style and an impulse_buy_probability drawn from that style's observed range).
The prompt revision string is unchanged (observe-plan-v5-unique-checkout) although the prompt now shows impulse_buy_probability and shopping_style and changes the IMPULSE instructions.
Both layouts and one catalogue appear in every split; no unseen-layout or unseen-SKU claim.
Corridor moves are down-sampled in training; navigation in deployment is still assisted by guided_nav_v3.
The 15 frozen benchmark shoppers are excluded, so the Layout A/B cohort is unseen during training.
